messages:
shreya: Quick heads-up — running int4 bring-up tests on magnet-13B with long anchored prefix + streaming prefill and I'm seeing deterministic token drift after ~4.2k tokens. Not a random flip, repeatable across seeds.

ben: ugh. is this only with RoPE scaling enabled?

shreya: yep, repro matrix:
- fp16 baseline: clean
- int8: small noise but passes eval tolerances
- int4 + rope-scale: consistent divergence at the exact anchor boundary

koen: can you paste the minimal repro? might be a K/V alignment thing when prefill spans shard boundaries

shreya: minimal run (truncated):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/longctx/test_prefill_align.py::test_prefill_anchor_shift -k anchor -q 
# config used:
--model magnet-13B-int4
--rope-scale 1.15
--prefill-append true
```
Output snippet:
```
[INFO] prefill: prefix_len=4096, in_flight=128
[WARN] kv_write: shard=2 offset=0x7fffa12c, write_len=8192
[ERROR] token_mismatch at step=4210 expected="the" got="a"
```

marta: do we have a dump of the KV indices around the boundary? that error looks like a classic off-by-one when rotatory indices are reduced for quantized int4 packing.

shreya: uploaded kv-dumps to /mnt/ci/artifacts/4321987654/ (kv_index.{shard}.{seq}.bin). Also instrumented the prefill path to log per-token rot-pos used: shows a jump in the rotary phase multiplier exactly when crossing the shard map remap.

ben: hmm, could be two things: (1) kernel-level quant reorder (pack/unpack) that changes effective position encoding resolution; (2) our rope-scale transform applied before quantized linear projection vs after — order matters with rounding.\
koen: suggestion: re-run with rope-scale=1.0 but apply a post-quant linear rescale hack that compensates rounding, to isolate whether rot-phase arithmetic is the culprit. also try keep_prefill_shard=true to avoid remap.

shreya: running both now. quick diff of one failed trace (int4, rope=1.15) vs int4 rope=1.0 shows rot-pos values diverging by ~0.003 at token 4209 which accumulates into a different top-k at 4210.

harry: can you add an eval harness that computes per-token embedding cosine-sim against fp16 golden to get where drift crosses threshold? that'll let us pick a deterministic rollback point for fallback policy.

shreya: good idea — added embed-sim checkpoints to CI run. output: first drop below 0.999 at token 4187, top-k change at 4210. attaching snippet.

ci-bot: CI run 4321987654-int4-prefill (magnet-13B) completed: 1 failed test, logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/4321987654

marta: if it's correlated with shard remap, try a tiny experiment: keep exact fp16 positional multipliers in host memory (float32) and only quantize activations. If that fixes it, we know the issue is quantizing the rot multipliers.

ben: also check our sign-extension when unpacking nibble-aligned KV pages — previous incident had a similar symptom where one nibble got misaligned on a page boundary.

shreya: next steps I'm doing: (1) re-run with keep_prefill_shard=true; (2) run with post-quant linear-rescale; (3) host-only rot mult (no quantize). Will post results in ~30m. If any of you want the KV dumps, ping me and I'll share.

koen: thanks. if host-only rot fixes it we should add a deterministic unit test around rot-phase idempotence under quantization to catch regressions.

marta: filing a follow-up issue once repro is triaged: INF-rot-int4-prefill-anchor-shift.

shreya: posted preliminary results: host-only rot mult = PASS (no drift), post-quant rescale = PASS (small residual noise but within tolerances), keep_prefill_shard=true = PASS. Looks like quantizing the rot multipliers (or the order of operations) is where the error sneaks in.

ben: great find. sounds like a safe short-term mitigation: force rot multipliers to float32 in quantized builds and add a perf note. Long-term: fix quant pack ordering and add idempotence tests.

shreya: filing a PR with the tests + mitigation. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/8765

harry: nice work. can we add an Optimize rule to recommend pinning rot to fp32 for models > 8k prefills until we patch? customers with longcontext will appreciate the opt-in. :thumbsup:

shreya: will add a config toggle in the model profile. thanks all.
